subject: data/signal_candidates.csv
reason: A handoff, not shared ownership. signal_harvest.py writes the queue; promote_signal_candidates.py consumes it and rewrites what remains, so the file holds exactly the rows the gate did not promote. The two never write concurrently: the promoter runs after the harvester in the same workflow.

subject: master_opposition.csv
reason: The source of record for Layer C, and the one file with more than one writer by design. scripts/build_master_csv.py refreshes it from upstream under the ownership rule that ended the 2026 corruption; census_gap_candidates.py and promote_signal_candidates.py append gated promotions only. All three are append-or-refresh under a stated ownership discipline, none of them rewrites another's rows, and every promotion lands in an audit trail. This exemption is the reason the rule exists elsewhere: it is the exception that had to be argued for.

subject: census_gap_candidates.py
reason: Layers C and D. This is the gap-closure promotion path: a Layer D census gap becomes a Layer C opposition record. The crossing is the point of the module and it is gated (complete, dated, sourced, dedup-guarded, census-corroborated), appends only, and writes every promote, hold and block decision to data/gap_promotion_report.csv.

subject: signal_harvest.py
reason: Layers A and C. One GDELT call returns both facility-lifecycle articles and opposition coverage, and splitting the network call in two would double the quota cost to separate what a single classifier can route. The module routes, it never merges: a row lands in exactly one layer's file, with the opposition side winning any tie, and neither file is a source of record.
